## New Features

- Follow thread links from search results and transcripts to open saved conversations and nested agents in the terminal. (#62332)
- Press `Tab` to complete arguments for supported slash commands. For example, `/mcp lo` completes to `/mcp login`. (#62343)

## Bug Fixes

- `codex exec resume` restores saved sandbox permissions, the working directory, and workspace roots unless explicitly overridden. (#62194)
- Remote sessions preserve working directories, workspace roots, and writable paths when the client and server run on different operating systems. (#62375, #62376, #62377)
- Codex reports provider errors as soon as they arrive in a response stream and identifies which API spend limit was reached. (#62329, #62356)
- Interrupting a parent turn preserves queued replies from child agents for the next turn. (#62348)
- Use `PageUp` and `PageDown` to read and submit answer choices that are taller than the terminal’s answer area. (#62209)
- Cloud replies that finish after history loads now update in place, keeping the terminal transcript in order. (#62403)

## Documentation

- The bundled `openai-docs` skill now covers migration to GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, including endpoint choices and t

## Desktop

### Improvements
- OpenCode 1 now offers the upgrade to OpenCode 2.0. OpenCode 2 downloads in the background and installs only when you choose: Restart to upgrade, Upgrade on quit, or Later. Your sessions, projects, and settings are kept. Plugins made for OpenCode 1 need an update.

## Core

### Bugfixes
- Sessions with many images no longer send oversized requests. When the images in a session's history pass 25 MiB, the oldest are replaced with a placeholder.
- A provider error for a request body that is too large now starts compaction and a retry instead of failing the turn.

### New Features

- **Decision models in codemode**: GitHub Copilot's `gpt-6-luna-decisions` and Radius decision models can be called from codemode `models.classify()`, and results include the provider's `responseId`. See [Classify](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.6.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/codemode.md#classify).
- **One setting per transcript notice**: cache misses, cache warming, compaction costs, and reasoning drops each have their own setting under Notices in `/settings`. See [Model and thinking](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.6.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md#model-and-thinking).
- **Dialog status kind for extensions**: `ctx.ui.select()`, `ctx.ui.confirm()`, and `ctx.ui.input()` accept `blockedKind`, so terminals with program status can show a dialog as a permission request, question, or login. See [Program Status Kind](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.6.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md#program-status-kind).

### Breaking Changes

- Replaced the `showCacheMissNotices` setting with one setting per transcript notice: `notices.cacheMisses`, `notices.cacheWarming`, `notices.compactionCosts`, and `notices.reasoningDrops`, configured under Notices in `/settings`. An existing `showCacheMissNotices` value is migrated to all four. `SettingsManager.getShowCacheMissNotices()` and `setShowCacheMissNotices()` are removed; use `getNotices()` and `setNotice()` instead

### Added

- Added `compat.supportsStrictMode` for `google-generative-ai` and `google-vertex` models in `models.json`, so Gemini 3+ models served under IDs

## Most of AutoCua now runs in Rust

Since 0.2.0 most of the agent code has moved from Python to Rust. Rust is now the largest language in the repository (about 45%, up from 23% in 0.2.0). It still ships prebuilt in the wheel, so you never need Rust. Each part was compared with the Python it replaced, case by case, before the switch.

- **Computer use:** one Rust agent now runs on macOS, Windows and Linux in place of three Python agents. Each system keeps its own prompts. Windows picks up what its copy had fallen behind on, such as the "Pure vision first" hint and the newer URL finder for site skills.
- **iPhone agent:** the agent, its controller (taps, typing, scrolls, opening apps, the shell, the video player, notes and the todo list) and its tool registry.
- **LLM layer:** the manager every agent sends its requests through, the Responses route and all eleven model providers.
- **Shared tools:** web search, the shell, the browser sub-agent and the Android sub-agent are now one copy each for every system, in `AutoCua/universal_tool`. They replace six copies of the web tool and fifteen copies of the others.
- **Also in Rust:** the tool registries, notes and todo lists for macOS, Windows and Linux, the vault, memory compression and the app's chat memory.
- The shell tools of computer use and the iPhone agent now run in the coder's sandbox. The old Python sandboxes are gone.
- The screen and phone readers, the desktop controllers and the app itself are still Python.

The version jumps from 0.2.0 to 3.0.0 to mark this move. There is no 1.x or 2.x.

## Security fix

With the ReAct runner (`runner: react`), `ReactConverter` fell back to Python `eval()` on the model's `Action:` text whenever it was not valid JSON. A prompt-injected action (from a web page, tool result or document the agent reads) could execute arbitrary Python on the host. Actions are now parsed with `ast.literal_eval` and must be a dict with `name` and `arguments`. Reported through TSRC.

The default `openai` runner is not affected. Upgrade if you use the ReAct runner.

## ⚠️ Breaking change

**The frontend no longer reads `TRUST_X_FORWARDED_FOR`** (#16530, @Pwuts). A self-hosted frontend that set it by hand gets no client IP from `X-Forwarded-For` for the sign-in IP log, IP blocks and per-visitor store search until `TRUSTED_PROXIES` lists the proxy in front of it. The single-container image and Vercel need nothing.

**What to do:** if your frontend sets `TRUST_X_FORWARDED_FOR`, remove it and set `TRUSTED_PROXIES` to a comma-separated list of the addresses or CIDR ranges of the proxies in front of it. Until you do, the frontend logs a warning at start that the old setting is ignored.
